technique.murim.twenty_four_plum_dome.we: The Dome stands where it was planted, and only in front: it does not guard the back, the sky above or the space inside. Step out from behind the trunks and the lattice falls apart. While it holds, the sword is busy - no strikes.
book.murim.six_harmonies: Six Harmonies Sword is the first teaching of Mount Hua. Foot accords with knee, waist with shoulder, breath with intent. Raise the blade above your head and bring it straight down upon the foe, lending the blow your body's weight. Do not reach with arms alone: the step must carry the sword, and the exhalation complete its course. This simple art teaches a firm foundation. Yet remember: a raised shoulder betrays the blow before steel falls. Do not stand before the foe with your sword held high.
book.murim.seven_plum_basic: Seven Plum Blossoms Sword grows from the foundations of Mount Hua swordsmanship. No blossom grows without a sturdy branch: first learn to cut, thrust, and return the blade to your chest. Guide the point from the waist. Join your blows with even breathing and small steps. Let each stroke prepare the next, while the free hand keeps your balance. Do not chase a beautiful trail. The sword's blossom opens only where steel can reach; if the foe retreats, first close the distance, then continue the sequence.
book.murim.seven_plum_blossoms: Settle into your stance, gather your breath, and unfold seven blossoms of the blade before you. Strike along the chosen line before the foe retreats.
book.murim.seven_plum_whirlwind: Circle the blade around your body, raising a ring of pillars. Hold the circle's heart as their walls draw together and imprison the foe.
book.murim.seven_plum_execution: Gather images of the swordsman around a chosen point and send them into a converging strike. Choose ground where the foe will linger.
book.murim.seven_plum_rush: Gather your breath at length in a motionless stance, then release a hurricane of blades straight ahead. Align the path of your onslaught beforehand.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_rainfall: Raise the sword and call down a shower of cutting petals from the sky. Keep the foe close beneath open heavens, or the blossoms will scatter.
book.murim.falling_petal_sword: Falling Petal Sword belongs to the art of Mount Hua: the petal yields to the wind, yet still finds the earth. Begin your advance from the side. Step in a circle to the left, passing around the foe toward his back. The blade must follow the turning waist, so the feet's motion flows into the blow without a needless swing. Do not halt before another's point or change your arc midway. A brief pause follows the turn; if the foe has gone the other way, recover your stance before closing again.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_step: Dark Fragrance Step is a lightness art of Mount Hua. As plum fragrance passes between branches, the swordsman slips through danger in a short dash. Lower the waist slightly, shift your weight onto the leading foot, and exhale with the push. Your gaze must choose the resting place before your feet leave the earth. Do not mistake swiftness for readiness: after the dash, the body needs a moment to gather its stance again. Leave room for this recovery.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_trail: The Fragrance Trail carries on Mount Hua's lightness art. Gathered breath bears the swordsman forward in a swift, unbroken run, like fragrance following a mountain path. Lean your body, keep your stride even, and choose a clear way ahead. Once you have crossed the needed distance, quiet your strength and end the run by your own will. Do not wait for a wall to end the path. A straight trail is seen from afar: a watchful foe will know your course and meet you with steel.
book.murim.dark_fragrance_behind: Fragrance Behind the Back is Mount Hua's circling step. Choose a foe with your gaze and guide your breath along an arc, moving swiftly to his back. Do not turn the shoulders alone: feet and waist must carry the whole body around him. Keep your sword ready for the next action from the moment you begin. Remember, watchful eyes can follow the arc, and the foe may meet you at its end. With no chosen foe, this art gives only a short step forward.
book.murim.wind_god_steps: God Wind has four forms: Dark Shadow conceals your approach, Lightning Flash is a short dodge, Netherworld King advances through an opening, and Star Light sustains a fast run. All four share one mastery. Practice any form to improve the whole art; greater mastery reduces qi expenditure. The tenth star completes the art: Star Light accelerates for one second, then reaches 30 blocks per second before external bonuses. Choose a clear path. Obstacles still stop you and your qi is finite.
book.murim.wind_god_shadow: Dark Shadow conceals your approach, sharing mastery with the other three God Wind forms. It unlocks at the first star. Higher stars reduce qi per second, extend concealment and fool more observers. At ten stars it affects up to twelve supported observers: zombies, skeletons and creepers. It does not end an existing chase; nearby contact, a strike or injury reveals you. Stay at least two blocks away. This is concealment, not invulnerability.
book.murim.wind_god_death: Netherworld King is the advancing form of God Wind, unlocked at the fourth star. Select an opening and pass toward or through your target. The distance increases from five blocks to eight at the summit; qi cost decreases with shared mastery. Without a target, the same advancing step follows your chosen direction. It grants no invulnerability and deals no extra damage. Prepare your next attack and watch for walls.
book.murim.wind_god_lightning: Star Light is the sustained run of God Wind. Gather speed over the first second and keep a clear route ahead. Mastery improves speed, duration and qi efficiency; ten stars give 30 blocks per second after acceleration. Body training extends the run, and pill discounts still apply. A strike or exhausted qi ends the run. Rest briefly before starting again. Lightning Flash, the dodge, is a separate form sharing this mastery.
book.murim.demon_palm: Demon Destruction Palm is a cruel art of the Demonic Sect. It gathers inner strength in the palm and releases it through a close blow. Root your feet, turn your waist, and carry force from the belly through the shoulder to the heel of the palm. Keep the fingers together and the wrist straight; do not push with arms alone. First enter touching distance, then unfold your strength. This art offers no distant strike: a palm extended into empty air leaves you open to the answer.
book.murim.seven_plum_blossoms.full: Before the plum can blossom, the branch must become still. Root your feet, quiet your shoulders, and gather breath at the hilt. Then unfold the blade's blossoms before you and bring their cuts together along the chosen line. Do not seek the foe with your point once they open: the blow's path is already laid. Strike as he finishes a step or is forced to stand and fight. One who knows this stance will move aside before the flowering. Hide your preparation behind his swing, and do not stand exposed without need.
book.murim.seven_plum_whirlwind.full: Guide the sword around your body, like wind circling an ancient plum tree. Pillars will rise from the turning motion, and walls between them will begin to close. Hold the center yourself: from there, you can press the foe toward the narrowing edge and hinder his escape. Do not expect the ring to become a prison at once. While gaps remain between the walls, a nimble foe can leave the circle. Begin the whirlwind where his steps are already confined, and keep him within until it closes. Long flowering demands patience.
book.murim.seven_plum_execution.full: Do not pursue the body; choose the ground where it will linger. Gather images of the swordsman around that place and direct them inward. Their blades will converge like branches above a narrow trail, leaving little room for defense. Yet the image obeys intent, not sight: it will strike the appointed point even after that point is empty. Catch the foe after a heavy swing, beside an obstacle, or in a cramped passage. One who leaves the gathering place in time will leave your swordsmen only dust.
book.murim.seven_plum_rush.full: For the onslaught, stand motionless and gather breath at length, allowing no tremor in the point. Align the path beforehand: the released hurricane of blades will rush straight ahead and will not turn after the foe. Let your gaze measure the passage, not his face. This form best meets one who advances toward you or is confined by walls. On open ground, preparation betrays your intent. Seeing the stance, the foe has time to leave its path. Do not release stored strength into emptiness merely because you have waited long.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_rainfall.ful: Raise the sword as though opening a road to heaven for the branches, and summon a shower of cutting petals. The blossoms fall from above; fight where no roof shelters the foe. Stay close and press him with short blows, denying him escape from the rain. Do not trust heaven's cut at every distance: far away, the images lose their shape and scatter. Beneath a roof, the petals cannot reach flesh. Draw the foe beneath open skies before raising your blade.
book.murim.ceremonial_draw: The nameless master taught: a sheathed sword is like a word still held back. Quiet your shoulders, hide intent within your breath, and let the foe approach. Then the scabbard releases steel, and the draw cuts the space before you before he recognizes the blow. Do not adorn the motion with a bow: silence performs the rite. Yet remember the price of resolve. Once begun, the draw cannot turn aside. If the foe leaves the blade's path, your hand will finish its promise, and his answering blow will find you.
book.murim.crescent_sweep: The nameless master likened this sweep to a sickle above an autumn field. Guide the blade in a broad arc before you to reach those pressing from different sides. Do not chase every point: one motion meets all who enter its reach. Strength rises from the body's turn; the hand merely guides the harvest. Yet the sickle bares the reaper's chest. The broad arc lowers your guard. One who waits beyond the blade's reach can step inside and strike before your sword returns.
book.murim.shadow_step: The nameless master said: the shadow conquers distance while the eye seeks the body. Gather your breath, slip from your former place, and arrive where the foe has yet to ready his blade. This step serves both approach and escape: change your position before another's steel completes its course. Do not take disappearance for invulnerability. At the step's end, your flank lies open: the foot has found earth while the body still follows. If the foe guesses where you will appear, his weapon will meet you before yours meets him.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_sea: Plum blossoms meet every flying blade, wrap around it and lay it on the ground. The master stands like a root and guides the sea with his gaze.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_sea.full: Softness that tames force. A single bud opens on the sword's tip, and blossoms drift from the blade — one, two, then a boundless sea close to the ground. Every arrow and every blade that enters it sinks: a blossom wraps the steel, holds it for a breath and lays it in the grass. Guide the sea with your gaze, but remember: it turns slowly, and its blossoms suffice for only a few projectiles in a volley. The master's feet are rooted and his blade is busy — up close he is defenceless. Whoever holds the sea longer than due pays with blood on his lips.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_river: Mount Hua's petals surge along the chosen line, sweeping away the foe. While the current gathers, the master stands still, and the sword's path is already fixed.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_river.full: Mount Hua's sword teaches: a fallen blossom is not dead while wind carries it above the river. Stand still, gather breath, and choose beforehand the path along which the petals will pour. Long silence becomes a torrent of swords: it rushes forward along the appointed line and falls upon the foe who remains before you. Yet the river will not turn after a fugitive. While preparing the blow, your body stands motionless within reach of another's steel. Should the foe leave the chosen path or shelter behind a stone, the fearsome torrent will scatter without reaching him.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_scatter: Mount Hua's petals ripen in blue flame. Spectral doubles cut the foe's former place; a blow while they gather will scatter the blossoms.
book.murim.twenty_four_plum_scatter.full: Mount Hua's plum scatters its blossoms, and each petal bears the sword's intent. Stand within blue flame, gathering petals until your breath fills them with strength. Then release spectral doubles: they bring their blades down where the chosen foe stood. Thus many images converge in one strike, hiding the true hand among the blossoms. Yet first the flowers must ripen. While gathering, you stand motionless; a foe's blow will interrupt the preparation and break the technique. One who leaves his former place will leave the doubles only emptiness.
book.murim.wedge_fan: The nameless master taught that strength should unfold like a fan in a wanderer's hand. Send sharp wedges spreading forward before you: they reach foes across a broad front and force a tight formation to seek gaps. Do not gather all intent into a single point; let each wedge carry its share of the blow. Thus it is easier to meet advancing foes than pursue a fleeing one. Yet the fan knows no winding paths. The wedges shatter against any obstacle. A foe behind wall or stone will preserve his flesh, while you spend your breath in vain.
book.murim.style.twenty_four_plum: For a hundred years this sword was thought lost. Twenty-four movements are not twenty-four strikes but twenty-four ways to open a flower. Whoever has not passed the Seven Blossoms will see only fine words here. Study in order: each movement is built on the one before, and none forgives haste.
book.murim.seven_plum_explosion: Draw the blade slowly down and back, gathering petals on its tip, then release them in one rising blow as a blast toward the enemy.
book.murim.seven_plum_explosion.full: The last of the seven forms gathers all the earlier ones taught. Draw the blade slowly down and back to your right leg without hurrying the breath: let the qi flow to the tip and the petals fly to it on their own. Hold the sword low for a heartbeat only. Then, with half a step, cut upward through the air, and the whole gathered plum bursts at the top of the blow where the blade looked, even toward an enemy in the sky. But the long wind-up is seen from afar: a sharp-eyed foe leaves the line before the blow, and behind a stone the petals cannot reach him.
technique.murim.seven_plum_shower.weakne: A long coil and a straight dive: break the master in his stance or step off the line of the dive.
book.murim.seven_plum_shower: Coil like a bowstring, push off from afar and pierce the enemy from above: you yourself become the point, and a rain of cuts pours after you.
book.murim.seven_plum_shower.full: Plum Blossom Shower is a thrust in which the whole body becomes the sword. Coil in the stance until light gathers at the hand, and hold it; do not release it early. Push off from afar, rise above the enemy and fall on him at a slant, point first: pass through him, do not stick in him. A shower of parallel cuts pours after you, and below a white flash breaks. A target caught by your gaze freezes even in the sky. The form's weakness is the long coiling and the straight path: it is easier to strike the master in his stance or step off the line of the dive than to withstand the blow.
book.murim.style.seven_plum: The Seven Plum Blossoms Sword is the root of the Mount Hua sword. The blossom does not strike with force: it opens where the enemy does not expect it, and its seven petals are seven ways to open. First learn the style itself: the steps, the grip and the three strikes from which every form grows. Only when the hand stops thinking about the sword will the first form open, and after it the next, each harder than the last. Do not hurry: a blossom opened before its time withers.
technique.murim.tang_five_thunders: Tang Clan: Five Successive Lightning Strikes
technique.murim.tang_five_thunders.weakn: The blades fly straight and aim at the moment of release: a sidestep between them breaks the chain. The throw weakens with distance.
technique.murim.tang_twelve_daggers.weak: A long motionless preparation; a dagger stops at the first body and at walls; the twelfth from the sky is announced by the master's leap.
technique.murim.tang_seven_stars.weaknes: The net is open toward the master: when the stars flare, step forward and the blades meet behind you. Stone across a qi thread drops its star.
technique.murim.tang_dark_burst.weakness: The slow dagger warns by its writhing and can be struck down; the dash is a straight line; the recall line shows as a qi thread.
book.murim.style.tang_daggers: The Tang Clan of Sichuan carries no sword in sight. Its weapons are blades as thin as willow leaves hidden in the sleeve, and a hand that lets them go before the enemy sees it move. Twelve throws make the art: eleven are known, the twelfth is the family's secret. Learn them in order: each throw stands on the one before it. Remember what is said of the Tang: a thrown blade is hard to call back.
book.murim.tang_five_thunders: Five blades almost at once, fanning out and closing in from different sides on one point: the first meets the guard, the fourth breaks it, the fifth kills.
book.murim.tang_five_thunders.full: Five Successive Lightning Strikes is the fifth throw of the Tang. One whip of the wrist and five blades fan out almost at once, then each turns toward the enemy from its own side. The first meets the guard, the second pushes the blade aside, the third opens a gap, the fourth breaks the defence, the fifth goes for the kill. Lead your hand: all five into one man and the chain breaks his shield; into many and you hold back a crowd. But the farther the enemy, the weaker the throw.
book.murim.tang_twelve_daggers: Eleven blades open in a fan against every foe at once; the twelfth the master throws from above, leaping toward the sun.
book.murim.tang_twelve_daggers.full: Twelve Flying Daggers is the name of the whole Tang art. One by one the blades slip from the sleeves and gather between the palms into a spinning flower; the enemy cannot tell which blade is which. A flick of the wrist and the fan opens: the blades fly in arcs, cross each other and find everyone who stands in front. Their edges carry the family's poison. Yet a body or a stone stops a blade, and the long preparation leaves the master open. The twelfth throw is the secret: the master leaps against the sun and strikes from above while the enemy still watches the fan.
book.murim.tang_seven_stars: Seven blades hang like stars behind and beside the enemy and meet in his throat at once: whoever retreats dies.
book.murim.tang_seven_stars.full: Soul-Stealing Seven Stars is the seventh throw, Tang Hyeol's favourite. The sleeves spread wide and seven blades fly out of both at once. They do not strike at once: they hang around the enemy like the stars of the Dipper and follow him if he backs away. Whoever retreats walks into the stream and takes a blade in the throat. The master decides when the stars fall: earlier is weaker, later is surer. But the net is open on the master's side, and whoever steps forward when the stars flare leaves the meeting point behind his back. Stone across a thread drops its star.
book.murim.tang_dark_burst: A slow dagger writhes like a living carp, then tears forward with the sound of the sky collapsing.
book.murim.tang_dark_burst.full: The Hidden Explosive Dagger is the eleventh throw. Qi is poured into the blade and it writhes like a living carp, flies slower than rain and raises dust in a whirl, until with the sound of the sky collapsing it tears forward, black and white, and bursts with qi. Throw a second dagger after it: it strikes the first and doubles its momentum. A blade that was deflected or dodged hangs in the air, and the master calls it back along a new line: the Dagger That Severs the Line of Life. The slow blade can be struck down.

technique.murim.tang_three_instant: Tang Clan: Three Blades of One Instant
technique.murim.tang_three_instant.weakn: The blades fly to where you will be: stop or turn back at the moment of the throw and the meeting point is empty. A sidestep does not help.
technique.murim.tang_flash_life.weakness: There is no force in the blade, only speed. Dodge on the master's gesture, not on the blade; a body or stone on the line stops it.
technique.murim.tang_sleeve_return: Tang Clan: Blades Return to the Sleeve
technique.murim.tang_sleeve_return.weakn: Nothing to call back without misses. An enemy is safe if he does not stand on the straight line between the master and the stuck daggers.
book.murim.tang_three_instant: Three blades: one straight, two from the sides and faster; all arrive at the same instant where the enemy will be.
book.murim.tang_three_instant.full: Three Blades of One Instant is the first throw of the Tang. "One came straight at him, and the other two spun toward him from the sides. Those that spun were much faster." The master throws at where the enemy will be, not where he stands: whoever runs or charges walks into all three blades at once, and a sidestep does not help, for arcs close both sides. There is one escape: stop or turn back at the moment of the throw. A deep master bends one of the arcs at a right angle.
book.murim.tang_flash_life: No force in the blade, only speed: it vanishes from the hand and appears right before the enemy's face.
book.murim.tang_flash_life.full: The Flashing Life-Taker is the sixth throw. "There was no great force in this dagger. It was simply speed. The dagger vanished as it left the hand and appeared right in front of him." It is not a killing throw but an interrupting one: throw it into the enemy's wind-up and the wind-up breaks. Watching the blade is useless against it: dodge on the master's gesture, on the flick of his fingers. Masters of the highest star send a second blade after the first, one without qi that cannot be sensed.
book.murim.tang_sleeve_return: Your misses are not lost: a dagger that misses sticks in the ground for 15 seconds. Press R and every stuck dagger within 20 blocks flies straight back to you, hitting each enemy on its line.
book.murim.tang_sleeve_return.full: Blades Return to the Sleeve. What to do: when you miss, the daggers stay stuck in the ground, glinting, for 15 seconds. Stand so the enemy is between you and them, then press R. What happens: every stuck dagger within 20 blocks tears free and flies straight back into your sleeve; each one hits any enemy standing on its line. Why: every miss becomes a second hit, and daggers you threw by hand come back to your inventory. Canon, ch. 195: "all the throwing blades lying on the ground were returned to his sleeve."

dialogue.murim.mentor.outsider: You're not one of ours. Sect books are for disciples. If you want to learn, go to the Leader at the sect gate, at the top of the trail.
dialogue.murim.mentor.who_outsider: Gyeong Pil. Six years now I've taught the children here to hold a sword like a brush. Join, and I'll teach you too.
dialogue.murim.mentor.first:
So, a new Yul. I am Gyeong Pil, I run the White Plum Hall. We don't teach fast here. We teach so it isn't forgotten.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.again: You again. Well, out with it.
dialogue.murim.mentor.opt.lesson: Do you have a lesson for me?
dialogue.murim.mentor.teach: The foundation. Six Harmonies, then the Falling Flower, then the first Seven Plum forms. Past that, the world teaches you. I hand over a book when I see the hand is ready.
dialogue.murim.mentor.lessons: A lesson isn't an errand. Do it, and I'll see it myself.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_given: Six Harmonies to the second star. Strike with the forms: the dummy, a real fight, a spar. Every honest swing counts.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_hint: Your Six Harmonies are at star %s; I need the second. Don't rush: finish the backswing, then strike. Clicking spam is not a strike.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_rank: The hand is ready, the body isn't. You get the Falling Flower when you break into the third rank. Meditate.
dialogue.murim.mentor.six_done:
I see it. Here: the Falling Flower Sword. Read it, then learn. And don't swing it in the kitchen. One more thing: the Leader wants a look at you. Go to him.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_given: Go to Seo Rang. Land three clean strikes in one bout, right after his swing, not before. Running in circles won't teach you anything.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_hint: He's fast because you watch the sword. Watch the shoulder. Let the swing pass, step aside, and strike while he's open.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_rank: Three clean ones, I saw. But the Seven Plums burn qi. Break into the second rank, then the book is yours.
dialogue.murim.mentor.spar_done:
Good. The Seven Plum Blossoms: the Cut, the Palisade, the Whirlwind. The sect gives you no more; seek the rest in the world. Elder Tae Rok asked for you; go and see him.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.beyond: I have nothing more to teach you. The higher forms lie in ruins and on steles. Bring me a question and I'll answer.
dialogue.murim.mentor.no_dantian: Without a dantian you can't hold qi; the words stay words. Meditate first: build your centre.
dialogue.murim.mentor.cut_locked: The Cut stands on the Seven Plum basics. Your art is at star %s; I need the fourth. Strike in chains until it's in your body.
dialogue.murim.mentor.secret_locked: The 24 Movements are a secret book. Below the Peak you can't grasp it, however you read. It's not a rule, it's your rank.
dialogue.murim.mentor.farewell: Go. And tomorrow, on the training ground before dawn.
dialogue.murim.leader.first: A traveller on Mount Hua. Rare, these days. What brings you to the gate?
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.become: I want to become a disciple
dialogue.murim.leader.who: Tae Hwi, leader of this sect. My sword is duller than the elders', but my memory for names is sharper. I'll remember yours too.
dialogue.murim.leader.question: Then one question. Why do you want the sword of Mount Hua?
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.ans_honest: I don't know. I want to find out
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.ans_plum: I want to see the plum bloom
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_strong: Honest, if foolish. Strength without roots breaks first. No matter, the mountain will teach you.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_protect: A good answer. Remember it when the sword grows heavy.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_honest: The best answer I've heard this year. Not knowing is an honest door.
dialogue.murim.leader.reply_plum: Ha. The plums here bloom every spring. The sword, less often. We'll see about yours.
dialogue.murim.leader.bow_prompt: The answer is no exam. Now bow to the ancestors of Mount Hua; they watch everyone who enters.
dialogue.murim.leader.after_bow: Good. One last thing: show me a single form of the Six Harmonies. There's the dummy; strike as you were taught.
dialogue.murim.leader.wait_form: The dummy is still waiting. One form, no more.
dialogue.murim.leader.form_seen: Clumsy. But honest, and the stance holds. That is enough to begin.
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.accept: Take the name of a disciple
dialogue.murim.leader.welcome: That is all. From today you are a disciple of Mount Hua, third generation: Yul. Go to Gyeong Pil; the Six Harmonies start with him. And eat well… if you can find anything.
dialogue.murim.leader.member: Ah, a disciple. How goes the training?
dialogue.murim.leader.sect_state: The roof leaks, the treasury is empty, a handful of disciples. But I know each of them by name and by handwriting. That's where we start.
dialogue.murim.senior.outsider: A stranger in the yard? Since you're here, can you hold a sword?
dialogue.murim.senior.greet: Junior. Back again? Itching for it?
dialogue.murim.senior.opt.lesson: The master said: three clean strikes
dialogue.murim.senior.accept: To half strength, then we bow. Don't go crying to the master after.
dialogue.murim.senior.accept_lesson: Clean ones, is it? Then wait for my swing. If you're quick enough.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused1: Cowardice is a choice too. Just don't make it a habit.
dialogue.murim.senior.refused2: As you wish. The yard isn't going anywhere.
dialogue.murim.senior.after_won: …Not bad. I yielded fairly. Don't let it go to your head; tomorrow will be different.
dialogue.murim.senior.after_lost: You watch the blade; watch the shoulder. Catch your breath and come again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line1: The master got us up before dawn again. My legs aren't mine anymore.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line2: They say bandits were seen on the trail again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line3: A hundred strikes on the dummy, then another hundred. That's the Six Harmonies.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line4: Don't let Senior Seo Rang catch you after lunch.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line5: The Leader was counting coins again. Porridge for supper, then.
dialogue.murim.disciple.line6: Someday our plum will bloom too. That's what the master says.

murim.sect.trial_form: The Leader nods: the form counts.
murim.sect.clean_done: Three clean strikes on the senior. Tell the master.
murim.sect.no_mountain: Mount Hua isn't in this world yet.
dialogue.murim.senior.parting: Seo Rang returns the bow: "Until tomorrow."
npc.murim.gatekeeper.title: Gatekeeper, third generation
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.outsider: Halt, traveller. This is the foot of Mount Hua. Past here there's only the trail and your own two feet.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.opt.become: I want to join Mount Hua
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.climb: You want to be a disciple of Mount Hua? Climb the mountain yourself; at the sect gate they will hear you out.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.far: A thousand steps up the cleft, then the ridge to the Golden Lock. Whoever gets there without turning back is already half one of us.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.no_carry: Carry you? Ha. The mountain tests you before the Leader does. Whoever can't climb it can't lift the sword either.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.member1: Ah, one of ours. Good road, fellow disciple. They're arguing about rice up top again.
dialogue.murim.gatekeeper.member2: Fellow disciple! Back before supper and I'll save you a flatbread.
dialogue.murim.mentor.where_leader: The Leader is at the sect gate, at the top of the trail. Go; he'll hear you.
dialogue.murim.leader.first_climbed: You climbed on your own, up the steps and not on someone's back. That's half the answer already. What brings you to the gate?
dialogue.murim.leader.where_mentor: Gyeong Pil is on the main terrace past the gate. Go; he is already waiting for new disciples.
technique.murim.tang_family_coins.weakne: Coins are light: a counter-swing of a weapon knocks them away, and a shield in front stops them. In open ground with nothing to bounce off and a single enemy, the coins are weak.
book.murim.tang_family_coins: Press R for a fan of bronze coins. A coin bounces off walls and floor, and from star 7 it hops to the next enemy after a hit.
book.murim.tang_family_coins.full: Tang Family Coins. Canon, ch. 210: "a technique that used coins; in the past only the heads of the Tang family could learn it." What to do: throw the fan at a wall next to the enemy or into a crowd. What happens: each coin hits for a little, ricochets off blocks (once from star 5, twice from star 9) and hops to a neighbour (from star 7). The fan grows: 3, 7, 12 and finally 18 coins. Why: it is the only Tang form that comes around corners and hits several enemies at once. Coins do not stick in the ground and do not come back.

dialogue.murim.disciple.formation3: Third form… no, fourth. Don't put me off!
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal1: Porridge and nuts. Again. They say it hardens the spirit.
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal2: Eat faster — after the bell the master won't wait.
dialogue.murim.disciple.meal3: Elder Tae Gyun put an extra scoop of porridge in my bowl today. Said he doesn't count food, he counts paper.
dialogue.murim.disciple.night1: Mm… dawn's soon. Let me sleep, brother.
dialogue.murim.disciple.night2: No wandering the yard at night. Formation at dawn — you'll oversleep.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening1: Evening is the only time my legs stop aching. Almost.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening2: Did you see senior Seo Rang fight today? Like painting a plum branch.
dialogue.murim.disciple.evening3: They say bandits were seen on the trail again.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training1: Spars to half strength, the poles, forms behind the ranks — whatever the master says. Sand for me today.
dialogue.murim.disciple.doing_training2: The plum blossom poles. Fall and you start again. I fell forty times.
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy1: Not now — I have a bout!
dialogue.murim.disciple.busy2: Later, later! Can’t you see we’re fighting?
dialogue.murim.disciple.opt.challenge: Spar with me? To half strength
dialogue.murim.disciple.challenge: With me? Fine. A bow, then to half strength. Just don't complain to the master.
dialogue.murim.disciple.joined: Go on, at the end. Watch the front row and strike with us.
dialogue.murim.second.formation1: Junior, the ranks are no place for chatter. Fall in or leave.
dialogue.murim.second.formation2: The front row keeps the beat. Watch my sword, not my face.
dialogue.murim.second.meal1: Seniors are served first. Get used to it.
dialogue.murim.second.meal2: I spent a year away from the mountain. Even this porridge feels like luxury now.
dialogue.murim.second.greet1: Junior. A bow to your senior — forgotten how it’s done?
dialogue.murim.second.greet2: Want to ask something — ask briefly. The sword is waiting.
dialogue.murim.second.greet3: Seo Rang was up before everyone again. Unbearable.
dialogue.murim.second.evening1: The grove is quiet in the evening. Qi flows smoother when juniors don’t interrupt.
dialogue.murim.second.evening2: Sit by me, if you can keep quiet.
dialogue.murim.second.night1: Night. Go to sleep, junior. Formation tomorrow.
dialogue.murim.second.bowed: Hm. Better. Maybe something will come of you yet.
dialogue.murim.second.challenge: A lesson? Fine. To half strength — and don't say I didn't warn you.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.formation1: Dawn formation costs nothing. The best thing this sect has.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.opt.ask: How is the sect faring, elder?
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.night1: Only spendthrifts burn candles at night. And me — over the ledger.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.greet1: Money doesn't grow on plum trees, disciple. Though some here seem to believe it does.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.greet2: Did you break something? No? Then why come to the Finance Hall?
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.answer: Debts in Huayin, the old books full of stains and holes, and paper gets dearer. But the sect stands. As long as every entry is honest, it stands.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.formation1: Watching the ranks. The second row is half a beat behind again.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.evening1: Evening is for rereading what your hands did by day.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.greet1: The Martial Hall is open to those who read, not those who flip pages.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.greet2: Show me your stance. …Shoulder up. Like that.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.answer: The foundation. The Six Harmonies — everything begins and ends with a six-part movement. The rest will follow.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.breakfast_dinn: Eat. An empty dantian can't hold qi.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.opt.ask: How do you treat injuries from training?
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.night1: At night they bring me those who trained in secret. Don't be one of them.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.greet1: Bruises again? Show me. Hm, you'll live.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.greet2: Herbs drying, the cauldron boiling. There is always work in the Medicine Pavilion.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.answer: Bruise salve and rest. Pills are for meridians, not for idlers who fell off the poles.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.night1: Go to sleep. I'll keep watch at the gate.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.opt.ask: What does the sect need, senior?
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.greet1: The sect gate is watched. The Leader ordered it — I stand.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.greet2: A newcomer? The Leader will receive you himself. And I'll take you to bow to the ancestors.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_tak.answer: People who stay when it gets hard. The rest we will earn.
dialogue.murim.elder.greet1: Study, disciple. The mountain remembers effort.
dialogue.murim.mentor.formation: Dawn means formation. Take the end of any row and follow the front rank, on the beat. Ten forms without a slip and the day will serve you well.
dialogue.murim.mentor.fall_in: Don't watch the sword — watch the shoulder of the man in front. Strike with him.
dialogue.murim.mentor.training: Sand, poles, forms. Everyone has his task. Why are you standing around?
murim.sect.morning.offbeat: Off the beat — watch the front row.
murim.sect.morning.done: Morning training complete: forms are learned faster today.

murim.page.wisdom: %s: nothing new, but reading settles the mind

murim.page.reread_wisdom: %s: you know this book by heart; reading it again settles the mind
murim.manual.reread_hint: You know all of it. Rereading wears the book out but brings insight.

murim.camp.cleared: The bandit camp is routed. Its loot is yours, and the band will not return.
command.murim.camp.reset: The camp is reset: the band will return when you come near

murim.sect.guard.warn_outsider: %s: "Outsiders go no further than the gate. Wait here; the Leader will come out himself."

dialogue.murim.opt.standing: What is my standing in the sect?
dialogue.murim.standing.line: You are a %s. Merit to the sect: %s.
dialogue.murim.leader.summoned: Gyeong Pil says you don't slack. Good. I've written your name in the book of disciples — don't let that line down.
dialogue.murim.leader.busy: Not now. Go to Gyeong Pil; he will tell you what to do.
dialogue.murim.leader.opt.ask_trust: Leader, I ask for the sect's trust.
dialogue.murim.leader.trusted: You climbed on your own and never left your own behind. From today you are trusted like a senior. Don't make me regret it.
dialogue.murim.tae_gyun.busy: Juniors come to me through their mentor. Go.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.busy: Juniors come to me through their mentor. Go.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.summoned: Gyeong Pil praises your sword. The Hall of Scriptures is open to you by day now; read, and leave others' things alone.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.opt.pass: Allow me to read in the Hall of Scriptures.
dialogue.murim.tae_rok.pass: Fifteen merit is not idle talk. Fine, by day you may enter. Not at night.
dialogue.murim.rise.novice: Pass Gyeong Pil's first lesson, or work: a rank and fifteen merit make you a third-class disciple.
dialogue.murim.rise.disciple: Three clean strikes on a senior: the mentor's lesson. Then you are a White Plum graduate.
dialogue.murim.rise.graduate: Thirty merit and the Leader's word. Trust is not handed out; it is earned.
dialogue.murim.rise.trusted: Above you there are only elders. You are trusted; do not squander it.
dialogue.murim.intercept_leader.stop1: Stop. The Leader is busy. Speak to your mentor, Gyeong Pil; he is on the dais by the square.
dialogue.murim.intercept_leader.stop2: Juniors see the Leader only when summoned. Go to Gyeong Pil, on the dais by the square.
dialogue.murim.intercept_leader.matter: Business goes to your mentor. If the Leader needs you, you will be summoned.
dialogue.murim.intercept_elder.outsider: You are not of the sect. The elders don't receive outsiders; wait for the Leader at the gate.
dialogue.murim.intercept_elder.stop: The elder does not receive juniors uncalled. Your mentor first.
dialogue.murim.intercept_elder.matter: Grow into the third class; then speak for yourself.
dialogue.murim.guard.greet2: Pass if you have business. If not, don't loiter at the door.
dialogue.murim.guard.night1: Night watch. Why are you wandering? Go to sleep.
dialogue.murim.guard.where_outsider: For you: as far as the gate. Beyond it, only the accepted.
dialogue.murim.guard.where_novice: The courtyard, the square, the camp, the grove. Not the seniors' halls; at night stay in the dormitory.
dialogue.murim.guard.where_disciple: By day: the Main Hall, the Ancestors' Hall, the treasury. Scriptures and the elders' houses are for graduates. At night, nowhere.
dialogue.murim.guard.where_graduate: By day, everywhere except the vault and the penance cave. At night the halls are closed.
dialogue.murim.guard.where_trusted: You are trusted. Go where you need. The vault only with the Leader.
dialogue.murim.steward.greet1: A sack of millet, two kegs of salt, rope... Did you bring something, or are you here to eat again?
dialogue.murim.steward.greet2: Elder Tae Gyun keeps the treasury. Stores, land and shops are on me.
dialogue.murim.steward.opt.estate: What does the sect live on?
dialogue.murim.steward.opt.help: I want to help the sect.
dialogue.murim.steward.night: The storeroom is locked at night. Come in the morning.
dialogue.murim.steward.estate: The shops in Huayin were ours once; the merchants took them while the sect grew poor. Now we carry everything up the steps ourselves: grain, salt, medicinal herbs.
dialogue.murim.steward.help: Gold, emeralds, grain: everything goes to use. I'll write the merit down to your name.
dialogue.murim.steward.thanks: Noted. Tae Gyun will circle it in red ink — that's his highest praise.
dialogue.murim.cook.greet1: The porridge is ready when it's ready. Don't hover over the pot.
dialogue.murim.cook.greet2: Grain and nuts, that's all the luxury there is. Eat and don't complain.
dialogue.murim.cook.answer: Millet with nuts. No meat, unless an elder sneaks some in again.
dialogue.murim.cook.night: The kitchen sleeps. So should you.
dialogue.murim.porter.greet1: A hundred steps with a sack on my back, then a hundred more. Make way.
dialogue.murim.porter.greet2: The guild brings it to the foot of the mountain; we carry it up.
dialogue.murim.porter.answer: The disciples run these steps for strength, I run them for rice. Same legs.
dialogue.murim.porter.night: Nobody carries loads on the steps at night; you'd break your neck.
dialogue.murim.gardener.greet1: Don't trample the beds. That's not a weed; it's medicine.
dialogue.murim.gardener.greet2: Gyeong Cho brews, but who grows it? I do.
dialogue.murim.gardener.answer: Bitter roots for wounds, leaves for fever. You can't brew pills out of words.
dialogue.murim.gardener.night: The herbs are asleep. Come by day.
dialogue.murim.sweeper.greet1: Plum petals fall every day. I sweep every day.
dialogue.murim.sweeper.greet2: A clean courtyard is the sect's face. Step aside, I'm sweeping.
dialogue.murim.sweeper.answer: Forty years I've swept this courtyard. I saw it burn and I saw it bloom again. I don't tire of it.
dialogue.murim.sweeper.night: At night only the wind sweeps, and old men who can't sleep.
dialogue.murim.water_carrier.greet1: Water from the well to the kitchen, from the kitchen to the healers. All day long.
dialogue.murim.water_carrier.greet2: Spill a drop and the cook will have my head.
dialogue.murim.water_carrier.answer: Never counted. As many as there are until sundown.
dialogue.murim.water_carrier.night: The well rests until morning. So do I.
murim.sect.guard.closing: %s: "%s is closing for the night. Leave while I'm still asking."
murim.sect.donate.enough: Steward: "That's enough for today. Bring more tomorrow."
murim.peddler.greet.0: Silver first, goods after. That is the way of the road.
murim.peddler.greet.1: I buy old books. What is written in them is not my concern.
murim.peddler.greet.2: Snow Plum pills, almost fresh. Almost.
murim.peddler.greet.3: Bandits are restless in the woods again. They say they carry pages torn from other sects' manuals.
murim.peddler.greet.4: A wooden sword for a disciple, daggers for the bold. Take your pick, young master.
murim.peddler.arrived: A travelling peddler has come to the village
command.murim.peddler.none: This is not a village: the travelling peddler does not come here
command.murim.peddler.info: Village centred at %s; the peddler's next visit in %s s
murim.training.exhausted: Your body is at its limit. Eat, sleep — then again.
murim.training.route.start.peak_climb: South Peak climb: no qi, to the top
murim.training.route.start.trail_sprint: Trail sprint: to the sect gate, no qi
murim.training.route.void: That was qi, not legs. Start over.
murim.training.tooltip.stone: Use with an empty hand to lift. Carry it uphill: every block up tempers the body.
murim.training.tooltip.slab: Hold it, look at the ground and crouch — push-ups with the weight on your back.
murim.training.tooltip.hint: Empty hands: crouch twice in rhythm — squats; stay down — horse stance; look at the ground and crouch — push-ups.
murim.rank.wall.body: Your qi has hit the wall, but your body would not survive the breakthrough. Temper it to stage %s
dialogue.murim.steward.opt.silver: Donate 5 silver taels to the sect
murim.junk_art.need_axe: You need an axe in hand
murim.junk_art.backlash: %s: the borrowed qi rebounds — weakness and a nosebleed
murim.junk_art.fake_grand: Of all the boasting about ten thousand dragons, one plain cut makes sense. You remember it.
technique.murim.village_brawler_fist.wea: The swing shows a mile off and any blow breaks it; skinned knuckles cost you a little health on every hit.
book.murim.village_brawler_fist: Written in a clumsy hand on the back of a tavern bill. Pull the arm back as far as it goes, so the whole street sees how strong you are, and throw it straight at the nose. If he hits first, start again. The author adds that his knuckles never healed.
technique.murim.green_forest_axe: Wild Axe of the Green Forest
technique.murim.green_forest_axe.weaknes: Only with an axe. The axe drags the body down: for two seconds after the chop you are slow and open.
book.murim.green_forest_axe: Mountain bandits of the Green Forest teach this to every new man in one evening. Raise the axe over the head, roar, and bring it down on whatever stands before you. There is no second movement. The book does not say what to do if the first one misses.
technique.murim.ten_thousand_dragons.wea: Two seconds of grand posing that even a flick interrupts, then one ordinary cut. There are no dragons.
book.murim.ten_thousand_dragons: Raise the sword to the heavens, where ten thousand dragons answer your call. Spread the left hand as a dragon spreads its wing. Stand on one leg as a crane among the clouds. Then cut. The dragons, it seems, are implied.
technique.murim.burst_breath.weakness: Eight seconds of strength on credit. Then the qi rebounds: weakness, nausea and a nosebleed (2 damage).
book.murim.burst_breath: Fill the chest until the ribs creak and force the qi into the arms all at once. The strength comes at once, and it is real. The bill comes later, and it is also real. The last page has a brown stain and the word "later" underlined twice.
technique.murim.bandit_rush.weakness: You crash into the crowd with no guard and then stand gasping for a second and a half.
book.murim.bandit_rush: Duck low, lead with the shoulder and run at him before he draws. Whoever is in the way falls down. You also fall down, more or less, but by then it is his problem. Best used with friends behind you.
technique.murim.sand_in_eyes.weakness: Almost no damage and a long cooldown; a true master is not fooled.
book.murim.sand_in_eyes: Not a martial art, and every orthodox sect will say so. Scoop up dust or sand while you seem to bow, and throw it into the eyes. A blind man cannot chase you. A master with his eyes shut still can.
murim.sect.log.last: Your last day on the mountain:
murim.sect.log.empty: No practice recorded yet. Join in whenever you like.
murim.sect.log.day_bonus: Full practice day: +%s merit. Total full days: %s.
murim.sect.log.chores: Two dawns without the formation. The mentor gave you kitchen duty: a bucket of water for Cook Kim in the camp kitchen. Until it is done, lessons earn no merit.
murim.sect.log.chores_done: Thank you for helping the kitchen. Other activities are optional.
murim.sect.log.verdict.away: Welcome back. Continue at your own pace; your progress is saved.
murim.sect.log.verdict.chores: Your duty is not done: a bucket of water for Cook Kim.
murim.sect.log.verdict.missed_formation: You missed the formation. In the rows the body learns what the head does not grasp yet.
murim.sect.log.verdict.missed_lesson: You missed the lessons. A bout, the poles, a lesson — anything.
murim.sect.log.verdict.full: Good. This is how Mount Hua lives: day after day.
murim.sect.log.verdict.streak: You have completed %s full practice days. Breaks preserve your diligence.
murim.sect.log.verdict.partial: Thank you for joining in. Continue whenever you feel like it.
murim.sect.meal.fed: Millet with nuts: never filling, but it keeps you going.
murim.sect.mentor.scold.1: The formation was at dawn. The Six Harmonies are the root of every Mount Hua technique: everything begins and ends with the six. Skip the root and you will have nothing to build on.
murim.sect.mentor.scold.2: Overslept? A sword not raised in the morning trembles in the evening. Tomorrow — front row, where I can see you.
murim.sect.mentor.scold.3: The body does not remember what you meant to do. It remembers what you did. This morning — nothing.
murim.sect.mentor.scold.4: For six years I have woken children at dawn. Those who got up now teach others. Think about it.
dialogue.murim.mentor.opt.why: Why all this — the formation, the schedule?
dialogue.murim.mentor.why: Practice builds the basics. Formation helps you find the rhythm, and you can also practise on your own. Return whenever you like.
dialogue.murim.mentor.opt.why2: And if I am stronger on my own?
dialogue.murim.mentor.why2: Strong swordsmen benefit from the basics too. Try six clean forms on your own or with the formation, whichever suits you.
dialogue.murim.mentor.scold:
The formation was at dawn, and you were not in it.
%s
dialogue.murim.mentor.opt.self_train: I train on my own. Why do I need the formation?
dialogue.murim.mentor.scold_ok: Your fault — so tomorrow you are first on the square. Go, lessons are still on.
dialogue.murim.mentor.chores: Two mornings without the formation. Duty: a bucket of water for Cook Kim in the camp kitchen. Do it, and we count days again.
dialogue.murim.cook.chores: If you would like to help, bring a bucket of water. It is optional; I will return the empty bucket.
dialogue.murim.cook.opt.water: Here is water for the kitchen.
dialogue.murim.cook.chores_done: Thank you, we can use the water. Enjoy your own projects and return whenever you like.
dialogue.murim.gyeong_cho.heal: Sit, hold still… A bruise, not a break. Ointment, a bandage — and no poles until evening.
murim.sect.log.rules: Gyeong Pil: "Join whenever you like: ten forms in time with the dawn formation, a bout, the poles or Tae Rok’s lesson by day, meals at the tables. Full practice days earn merit; seven of them, with any breaks, earn the leader’s approval. Adventures and your own projects cost you nothing. Your next step is in the log."
